questions.question: A newsvendor has integer demand $D$ with CDF $F(y)=\mathbb{P}(D\le y)$, unit cost $c$, salvage value $s<c$, price $p>c$, $b=p-c$, $h=c-s$ and $\beta(p)=\frac{p-c}{p-s}$. Price sensitivity keeps $y$, $c$ and $s$ fixed and asks for which prices $p$ the order $y$ stays optimal. Which condition describes these prices?
options: $F(y)\le\frac{p-c}{p-s}\le F(y+1)$
$F(y-1)\le\frac{p-c}{p}\le F(y)$
$F(y-1)\le\frac{p-c}{p-s}\le F(y)$
$F(y-1)\le\frac{c-s}{p-s}\le F(y)$

questions.question: A newsvendor has integer demand $D$ with CDF $F(y)=\mathbb{P}(D\le y)$, unit cost $c$, salvage value $s<c$, price $p>c$, $b=p-c$, $h=c-s$ and $\beta(p)=\frac{p-c}{p-s}$. The price $p$ rises while $c$ and $s$ stay fixed. How does $\beta(p)$ behave?
options: It stays constant, since $p$ appears above and below
It falls, since the denominator $p-s$ is the larger term
It grows in proportion to $p$ and can exceed 1
It rises towards 1, as $1-\beta=\frac{c-s}{p-s}$ shrinks

questions.question: A newsvendor has integer demand $D$ with CDF $F(y)=\mathbb{P}(D\le y)$, unit cost $c$, salvage value $s<c$, price $p>c$, $b=p-c$, $h=c-s$ and $\beta(p)=\frac{p-c}{p-s}$. A whole-number order $y$ is optimal exactly when $F(y-1)\le\beta(p)\le F(y)$. A shop uses this condition to find the price range over which ordering $y=10$ stays optimal. Which assumption does that analysis make?
options: The unit cost $c$ moves together with the price $p$
The salvage value $s$ is a fixed fraction of the price $p$
The order may take any fractional value near $y$
The demand distribution $F$ does not change with $p$

questions.question: A newsvendor with integer demand has $F(y-1)=0.25$ and $F(y)=0.40$ for some order $y$, where $F(y)=\mathbb{P}(D\le y)$. Unit cost is $c=20$, salvage $s=0$ and price $p=30$; $y$ is optimal exactly when $F(y-1)\le\frac{p-c}{p-s}\le F(y)$. Is $y$ optimal?
options: No, as $\frac{2}{3}$ exceeds $F(y)=0.40$
No, as the markup $0.5$ exceeds $F(y)$
Yes, as any price above the cost $c$ is allowed

questions.question: For a newsvendor with integer demand, fixed unit cost, salvage value and demand distribution, ordering 6 units is optimal exactly for selling prices $40\le p\le70$. The price is raised to $p=80$. Which order quantities can now be optimal?
options: Still 6, since demand is unchanged
7 or more, as the seventh unit pays
5 or fewer, as fewer customers buy
6, provided the salvage value rises

questions.question: A newsvendor has integer demand $D$ with CDF $F(y)=\mathbb{P}(D\le y)$, unit cost $c$, salvage value $s<c$, price $p>c$, $b=p-c$, $h=c-s$ and $\beta(p)=\frac{p-c}{p-s}$. A whole-number order $y$ is optimal exactly when $F(y-1)\le\beta(p)\le F(y)$. Unit cost is $c=12$, each leftover costs 3 to dispose of ($s=-3$), and $F(y)=0.8$. What is the highest price at which $y$ is still optimal?

A newsvendor has integer demand $D$ with CDF $F(y)=\mathbb{P}(D\le y)$, unit cost $c$, salvage value $s<c$, price $p>c$, $b=p-c$, $h=c-s$ and $\beta(p)=\frac{p-c}{p-s}$. A whole-number order $y$ is optimal exactly when $F(y-1)\le\beta(p)\le F(y)$. With $c$, $s$ and $F$ fixed, the price rises gradually from just above $c$ to a very high value. How does the smallest optimal order behave?
options: It grows smoothly and in proportion to the price $p$
It stays constant over price intervals and jumps up
It falls, since higher prices make leftovers costlier
It never changes, since demand is held fixed

questions.question: A newsvendor has integer demand $D$ with CDF $F(y)=\mathbb{P}(D\le y)$, unit cost $c$, salvage value $s<c$, price $p>c$, $b=p-c$, $h=c-s$ and $\beta(p)=\frac{p-c}{p-s}$. A whole-number order $y$ is optimal exactly when $F(y-1)\le\beta(p)\le F(y)$. For $y$ with $F(y-1)=0.5$, $F(y)=0.75$ and $c=30$, salvage rises from $s=10$ to $s=15$. How does the price interval for $y$ move?
options: Both endpoints move to higher prices
It stays the same, as $s$ only affects leftovers
Both of its endpoints move to lower prices
It widens, with endpoints moving apart

questions.question: A newsvendor has integer demand $D$ with CDF $F(y)=\mathbb{P}(D\le y)$, unit cost $c$, salvage value $s<c$, price $p>c$, $b=p-c$, $h=c-s$ and $\beta(p)=\frac{p-c}{p-s}$. A whole-number order $y$ is optimal exactly when $F(y-1)\le\beta(p)\le F(y)$. An order $y$ is found to be optimal at the prices $p=40$ and $p=60$. What follows for the price $p=50$?
options: $y$ is optimal at $p=50$ too, as $\beta(p)$ is increasing
It must be rechecked, since $\beta(p)$ is not linear in $p$
$y$ is optimal at $p=50$ only if the salvage value is 0
$y$ cannot be optimal at three different prices

questions.question: A dress costs 25 to buy plus 5 to handle per unit, so the effective unit cost is $c=30$; unsold dresses fetch $s=10$. For an order $y$ with $F(y-1)=0.5$ and $F(y)=0.75$, $y$ is optimal exactly when $F(y-1)\le\frac{p-c}{p-s}\le F(y)$. For which prices $p$ is $y$ optimal?

A newsvendor has integer demand $D$ with CDF $F(y)=\mathbb{P}(D\le y)$, unit cost $c$, salvage value $s<c$, price $p>c$, $b=p-c$, $h=c-s$ and $\beta(p)=\frac{p-c}{p-s}$. A whole-number order $y$ is optimal exactly when $F(y-1)\le\beta(p)\le F(y)$. Demand never exceeds 4, so for $y=4$ we have $F(3)=0.8$ and $F(4)=1$; also $c=10$ and $s=4$. For which prices $p>c$ is ordering 4 optimal?
options: No price, since $\beta(p)<1=F(4)$
Only prices of at most 34
Every price of at least 34
Every price above $c=10$

questions.question: A newsvendor has integer demand $D$ with CDF $F(y)=\mathbb{P}(D\le y)$, unit cost $c$, salvage value $s<c$, price $p>c$, $b=p-c$, $h=c-s$ and $\beta(p)=\frac{p-c}{p-s}$. A whole-number order $y$ is optimal exactly when $F(y-1)\le\beta(p)\le F(y)$. Here $c=40$, $s=10$, $F(5)=0.25$, $F(6)=0.75$ and $F(7)=1$. For which prices are both 6 and 7 optimal orders?
options: Every price of at least 130
Just one price, namely 130
Every price from 50 up to 130
Every price below 130

questions.question: A newsvendor has integer demand $D$ with CDF $F(y)=\mathbb{P}(D\le y)$, unit cost $c$, salvage value $s<c$, price $p>c$, $b=p-c$, $h=c-s$ and $\beta(p)=\frac{p-c}{p-s}$. A whole-number order $y$ is optimal exactly when $F(y-1)\le\beta(p)\le F(y)$. For some $y$, demand $y$ has probability 0, so $F(y-1)=F(y)=0.6$; also $c=40$ and $s=10$. For which prices is $y$ optimal?
options: For no price, since the interval is empty
For all prices with $\beta(p)$ near 0.6
Only at $p=85$, where it is the unique optimum
Only at $p=85$, tied with $y-1$ and $y+1$

questions.question: A newsvendor ($c=10$, $s=0$) faces demand with $F_A(6)=0.4$, $F_A(7)=0.6$, so 7 is optimal for $\frac{50}{3}\le p\le25$. Raising the price to 24 changes demand to $F_B(4)=0.3$, $F_B(5)=0.45$, $F_B(6)=0.65$, $F_B(7)=1$. The order is the first $y$ with $F(y)\ge\frac{p-c}{p-s}$. What should be ordered at $p=24$?
options: 7, since $\beta(24)$ still lies in $[0.4,0.6]$
8, since a higher price always calls for more stock
6, since the price change also changed the demand
5, since a higher price lowers the critical ratio

questions.question: A newsvendor has integer demand $D$ with CDF $F(y)=\mathbb{P}(D\le y)$, unit cost $c$, salvage value $s<c$, price $p>c$, $b=p-c$, $h=c-s$ and $\beta(p)=\frac{p-c}{p-s}$. A whole-number order $y$ is optimal exactly when $F(y-1)\le\beta(p)\le F(y)$. With $c=20$ and $s=0$, ordering 8 is optimal exactly for prices $40\le p\le60$. What is the probability that demand equals exactly 8?

A newsvendor has integer demand $D$ with CDF $F(y)=\mathbb{P}(D\le y)$, unit cost $c$, salvage value $s<c$, price $p>c$, $b=p-c$, $h=c-s$ and $\beta(p)=\frac{p-c}{p-s}$. A whole-number order $y$ is optimal exactly when $F(y-1)\le\beta(p)\le F(y)$. Assume $F(y-1)<F(y)$. The price equals the upper endpoint of the interval for $y$, so $\beta(p)=F(y)$. Which statement holds?
options: $y-1$ and $y$ have equal expected cost
$y$ ties with the larger order $y+1$ in cost
$y$ is no longer optimal at this price
$y$ is the only optimal order at this price

questions.question: A newsvendor has integer demand $D$ with CDF $F(y)=\mathbb{P}(D\le y)$, unit cost $c$, salvage value $s<c$, price $p>c$, $b=p-c$, $h=c-s$ and $\beta(p)=\frac{p-c}{p-s}$. A whole-number order $y$ is optimal exactly when $F(y-1)\le\beta(p)\le F(y)$. At the lower endpoint for $y$, $\beta(p)=F(y-1)$. How does $y$ compare with the smallest optimal order (the first quantity whose CDF value is at least $\beta$)?
options: $y$ is optimal, but not the smallest optimal order
$y$ is both optimal and the smallest optimal order
$y$ is not optimal, since $y-1$ is strictly cheaper
$y$ is the unique optimal order at that price
